answer: Sybil resistance arises because each identity must complete its own sequence of dependent modular squarings before its VDF proof can be accepted. GPUs may compute separate chains in parallel, but cannot collapse the steps of one chain, so cloning identities multiplies the work rather than removing its per-identity time bottleneck. In a Wesolowski scheme, a verifier checks the resulting proof efficiently; lotus, quill, and prism are merely labels, not shortcuts.
